question_reviews.actual_stem: After successfully boarding an Escape Pod, may you launch immediately rather than wait? When it launches now or on a later turn, what happens to the Pod token and occupants’ miniatures, and do those occupants continue taking part in active play?
question_reviews.requested_coverage: Post-boarding immediate launch option, launch removes Pod token and occupants' miniatures/active participation, while final checks remain.
question_reviews.actual_key: After boarding, choose to launch immediately or wait. Launching immediately or later removes the Escape Pod token and its occupants’ miniatures from the game; they no longer take part in active play. This does not establish victory: the already-covered final Contamination and Objective checks still apply.
scope_or_limit_notes: Physical launch removal and end of active play are expressly requested here. Under fixed Q19 scope they were correct extra context rather than that question's full required launch procedure.

findings.topic: Coolant Leak reconstitutes the Event deck even before deck exhaustion
findings.proposed_question: After resolving the illustrated Coolant Leak Event, the Event deck still has cards and the Generator has no Malfunction. Does the card merely go to the Event discard pile, or what happens to the card, remaining Event deck and Event discard pile? What changes if the Generator has a Malfunction?
findings.expected_answer: First resolve the normal matching-symbol Intruder movement. Coolant Leak starts Self-Destruct only if the Generator has a Malfunction. Independently of that condition, remove Coolant Leak from the game, then reshuffle the remaining Event deck together with its discard pile to form the Event deck. Do this even when the deck was not exhausted. With no Generator Malfunction the countdown is not started, but removal and reshuffling still occur. Do not shuffle the removed Coolant Leak back in.

raw_primary_support.location: lower-right illustrated Coolant Leak card; Example of an Event Card point 3
raw_primary_support.primary_passage: REMOVE this Event from the game and reshuffle the Events deck (including the Discard pile).
raw_primary_support.corroborating_prose: In this example, check if a Malfunction marker is present in the Generator Room to trigger the effect. Then, REMOVE this Event from the game (back to the box) and reshuffle the Event deck and discard pile.

closest_actual_branches.actual_stem: Give the Event Phase order, which Intruders move on an Event card, what controls movement and when the event effect resolves; what happens when Event and Intruder Attack decks run out?
closest_actual_branches.actual_key: Time and active Self-Destruct advance, Intruders in Combat attack, Fire Damage, Event card movement then effect, bag development fully resolved before next turn. Move symbol-matching Intruders without Characters in Room via card-number Corridor; ducts remove miniature/return token. Discard Event unless instructed otherwise. Empty Event/Attack decks reshuffle their respective discard piles.

closest_actual_branches.actual_stem: An Event instructs removing itself from the game but its other effect cannot be resolved. Is it removed?
closest_actual_branches.actual_key: Yes, remove it even if its other content cannot resolve.

closest_actual_branches.actual_stem: Can the Coolant Leak Event start Self-Destruct while someone hibernates, and how does that differ from starting it as a Character?
closest_actual_branches.actual_key: Yes, Event can; Character initiation is prohibited while anyone hibernates.

closest_actual_branches.actual_stem: Describe starting, stopping and restarting Self-Destruct, advancing it, the yellow threshold, its final space, a jump while active and a Character already hibernating.
closest_actual_branches.actual_key: Start marker first green; advance with Time. Stop removes it, restart green. First yellow irreversible/unlocks all Pods, which can relock; subsequent yellow spaces do NOT re-unlock them. Skull or jump with active sequence destroys ship. Characters cannot initiate sequence with anyone hibernating, but Coolant Leak Event can start it despite sleepers.

findings.distinct_consequence: Q24 asks ordinary Event-phase ordering and what happens when the Event/Attack decks run out; it keys reshuffling discarded Events only upon exhaustion. Q66 asks only whether a remove instruction still applies when other content cannot resolve. Q73/Q39 ask the sleeper exception and countdown mechanics. None requests reintegrating an existing Event discard pile into a still-nonempty deck. This is a distinct deck-management timing exception that changes which previously discarded Events may recur immediately, not a different cost/count/Character name or a recombination of the existing exhaustion rule. Generator condition/removal/sleeper context alone is not the novelty basis.
